metaDescription: Six 18 inch single stage snow blowers compared across gas, cordless and corded on clearing depth, throw distance, auger type and cold weather starting.
expertTake: The Poulan Pro 18 inch gas snow blower is the pick for most people with a typical driveway and snow that falls heavy, because a gas engine with cold start technology does not run down mid storm. The Westinghouse WSnow18 48V is the best cordless pick, with a rubber-tipped steel auger and a published snow rate. The Westinghouse WSnow18D corded is the value pick for short driveways near an outlet. If your driveway is long, steep or regularly buried under a foot of wet snow, skip every single stage machine and look at a two stage model.
introParagraphs: A single stage snow blower clears snow with one auger that scoops, throws and scrapes the pavement in a single motion. It is lighter and cheaper than a two stage machine, and it leaves a cleaner finish on a paved surface. The catch is that its depth and distance claims describe fresh, light snow, not the wet slush that follows a thaw.

This guide explains how auger design, power source and intake height affect real clearing, why battery runtime and cord length matter more than headline power, and what to check before buying for a gravel or steep drive. Start with the picks above for the short list, then read the reviews below to match a machine to your snowfall and your driveway.

products.name: Poulan Pro 18 Inch Single Stage Gas Snow Blower with Electric Start
products.description:
A gas engine solves the problem that limits most small snow blowers: runtime. The Poulan Pro uses a 99cc four stroke engine with cold start technology rated for starting down to -22 F, plus an electric start button so you do not have to haul on a recoil cord with cold hands. With an 18 inch clearing width and a 10.5 inch intake height it handles a typical driveway and sidewalk, and it keeps going as long as there is fuel in the tank.

The auger is steel reinforced rubber, which scrapes down to the pavement without chewing it up, and a one hand 190 degree remote chute control lets you aim the discharge without letting go of the handle. Compared with the Westinghouse WSnow18 48V, which publishes a rate of 650 pounds per minute but needs batteries recharged, the Poulan Pro trades silence and zero emissions for fuel and maintenance. Against the corded WSnow18D at 10 inches of depth, it has a slightly taller intake, and no cord to manage.

The machine rolls on two 7 inch never-flat wheels and carries a two year warranty. Ownership is where gas asks more: fresh fuel with stabilizer, an oil check before the first run, a clean spark plug, and a plan for storing it in a dry place. Keep a pull of the fuel line empty or add stabilizer at the end of the season, so the carburetor does not gum up. The listing also appears under a near identical title, which is the same machine.
products.bestFor: Owners of typical driveways who get frequent heavy snow and want a gas machine with electric start and no battery limit.
pros: Gas engine runs as long as there is fuel in the tank
Electric start and cold start technology down to -22 F
Remote chute control adjusts discharge with one hand
Never-flat wheels remove tire care from the list
cons: Needs fuel, stabilizer and seasonal engine maintenance
Louder and smellier than the electric picks
Intake of 10.5 in still limits very deep snow

products.name: Westinghouse WSnow18 48V Cordless 18 Inch Snow Blower Kit
products.description:
The WSnow18 is the most complete cordless kit in this lineup for one reason: the data. A 1200 watt brushless motor throws 650 pounds of snow per minute and clears an 18 inch wide, 10 inch deep path, and the listing states how long the batteries last: about 15 minutes for 7 inches of snow. That is honest, and it tells you this is a machine for a driveway of modest length, not a full lot.

Two 24V 4Ah lithium ion batteries combine into 48V, and a dual port 2.2A charger refills them in about 1.8 hours. The rubber-tipped steel auger is built to clear pavement without gouging it, the chute rotates 180 degrees, and dual LED lights light the path for early morning clearing. Compared with the Snow Joe kit, which quotes 14 tons of snow per charge and a 20 foot throw, the Westinghouse throws farther at 25 feet and states the minutes per charge.

The warranty is two years limited with lifetime technical support from a nationwide service network. Ownership is the simplest in the lineup: no fuel, no oil, no spark plug. Keep batteries indoors until you need them, since cold reduces output, and charge them before the forecast. For a bigger driveway, plan a second set of batteries, because a single set will run out before the job does.
products.bestFor: Owners of short to mid-length driveways who want a cordless machine with clear runtime and snow rate data.
pros: Published rate of 650 lb per minute and 25 ft throw
Brushless motor needs no brushes, oil or fuel
Dual LED lights help with dark early mornings
Two year warranty with lifetime technical support
cons: Runtime of about 15 minutes for 7 inches of snow limits long drives
Batteries lose output in deep cold if stored outdoors
Needs a second battery set for large driveways

products.name: Outsunny 40V 18 Inch Cordless Snow Blower with PU Auger

specList.label: Clearing path
specList.value: 18 in wide, up to 12 in deep

products.description:
The Outsunny stands out for two specs. Its clearing depth is up to 12 inches, deeper than the 10 inches claimed by the Westinghouse and Snow Joe machines, and its auger is polyurethane rather than steel. A PU auger flexes and absorbs impacts from hidden stones and does not scratch wooden decks, pavers or patios, which makes it the choice if you clear delicate surfaces.

A 1400 watt pure copper brushless motor on a 40V battery platform gives it the highest listed motor power in the cordless group, and two 4.0Ah batteries with two 2A chargers fill in about two hours at once. The chute turns 180 degrees with 60 degrees of vertical pitch adjustment, which controls how far the snow flies. The 21.3 foot maximum throw is shorter than the 25 feet of the Westinghouse, so plan where the snow lands.

A dual safety switch requires a two step start, and the machine folds for storage. Compared with the Snow Joe 24V-X2-SB18-TV1, it has a deeper path and a gentler auger, but a lesser known name and no warranty period in the data we have. Ownership is simple like any battery tool: warm the batteries indoors, charge both before a storm, and rinse salt off the machine after use.
products.bestFor: Owners of decks, pavers and wooden walkways who want a deeper clearing path and a gentle polyurethane auger.
pros: Up to 12 inches of clearing depth leads the 18 inch group
Polyurethane auger protects decks, pavers and patios
Two batteries and two chargers ship in the box
Vertical chute pitch adjusts throw height
cons: Throw distance is shorter than the Westinghouse WSnow18
Warranty terms are not stated in the data we have
Lesser known brand with a shorter record

products.name: IONMAX Snow Joe 48V 18 Inch Cordless Snow Blower Kit

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: Up to 14 tons of snow per charge

products.description:
Snow Joe quotes capacity in an unusual way: up to 14 tons of snow per charge. That is a ceiling for light snow, but it gives a feel for the scale of a driveway the kit can handle on one set of batteries. A 1200 watt brushless motor, an 18 inch wide by 10 inch deep path and a 180 degree chute that throws up to 20 feet are standard for this class.

The kit includes two 4Ah 24V IONMAX batteries that combine into 48V, a charger, a cover and a scraper. The cover and scraper are small touches that help with winter storage and clearing packed snow off the housing. Compared with the Westinghouse WSnow18, the Snow Joe offers the same 1200 W motor class and 10 inch depth, but a shorter 20 foot throw and no stated warranty period in the data we have. A 2 watt LED headlight handles dark mornings, although the Westinghouse has dual lights.

It is a single-stage machine meant for light to moderate snow, and a sibling Snow Joe GO model lists up to 700 pounds of snow per minute at the same 18 inch width. Ownership is the standard battery routine. Charge before the storm, store the batteries at room temperature and wipe the housing dry. For snow over a foot or very wet snow, it will need more passes.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a cordless kit with a cover and scraper included and a familiar snow tool brand.
pros: Cover and scraper come in the kit
Quoted capacity of up to 14 tons of snow per charge
Brushless motor with 180 degree adjustable chute
Familiar brand with a wide battery platform
cons: Throw distance of 20 ft is shorter than the Westinghouse
Single LED headlight is dimmer than dual light designs
Warranty period is not stated in the data we have

products.name: Westinghouse WSnow18D 18 Inch Corded Electric Snow Blower

specList.label: Start
specList.value: Push button, works in cold weather

products.description:
A corded motor is the one electric option with no runtime limit, and the WSnow18D uses the full draw of a household outlet. At 1800 watts and a quoted 720 pounds of snow per minute it posts higher numbers than the battery WSnow18's 650 pounds per minute, and it keeps that output for as long as you stay plugged in. It clears the same 18 inch by 10 inch path and throws snow up to 25 feet.

The cost is the cord. You need an outdoor rated extension cord of an adequate gauge, an outlet within reach, and the discipline to keep the cord out of the path of the auger. A cord retainer keeps the cable suspended and out of the way, and a push button start plus a squeeze lever make a two step start that works in very cold weather. Compared with the DEKOPRO 18 inch corded at 800 pounds per minute and a 9 inch depth, the Westinghouse is deeper and states a lower rate, but it has the brand and support behind it.

It rolls on 6 inch wheels and has dual LED headlights. Ownership is minimal: no fuel, no oil, no battery. Inspect the cord and the outlet connection before each storm, use a GFCI protected outlet, clear snow from the machine after use and store it dry. Choose it for short driveways, steps and walkways close to a source of power.
products.bestFor: Owners of short driveways, steps and walkways near an outdoor outlet who want unlimited runtime without fuel.
pros: No runtime limit while plugged in
Higher quoted rate than the battery WSnow18
Cord retainer keeps the cable out of the way
Two step push button start works in cold weather
cons: The cord limits reach and needs careful routing
Needs an outdoor rated extension cord and a GFCI outlet
Small 6 inch wheels roll less easily on rough ground

products.name: DEKOPRO 18 Inch 15 Amp Corded Electric Snow Blower

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Dual action switch, dual LED lights

products.description:
The DEKOPRO is the least expensive way into an 18 inch snow blower in this roundup. A 15 amp motor at 3,200 rpm moves up to 800 pounds of snow per minute and throws it as far as 25 feet through a 180 degree chute. The two blade steel auger clears a path 18 inches wide and 9 inches deep.

The 9 inch depth is the weak point. It is an inch shallower than the Westinghouse WSnow18D, so the DEKOPRO needs more passes after a heavy fall, and a steel auger deserves more care on delicate surfaces than the rubber-tipped augers of the Westinghouse or the PU auger of the Outsunny. The dual action safety switch asks you to press a lock before pulling the trigger, which helps with gloved hands and prevents accidental starts, and dual LED headlights cover dark mornings.

It is a corded machine, so the same cord rules apply: an outdoor rated extension cord, a GFCI outlet and careful cable handling. Ownership is minimal, but warranty and support details are thin in the data we have, so check the seller terms before buying. A good fit for a small porch, steps and a short walk.
products.bestFor: Budget minded owners with a small porch, steps and a short walkway near an outlet.
pros: Lowest cost way into an 18 inch electric snow blower
Quoted 800 lb per minute and 25 ft throw
Dual action switch prevents accidental starts
Dual LED headlights for dark mornings
cons: Nine inch clearing depth needs more passes in heavy snow
Steel auger needs care on decks and delicate surfaces
Warranty and support details are not stated in the data we have

buyingCriteria.explanation: A single stage blower is designed for fresh, light to moderate snow, and the depth figure is the maximum height it can swallow in one pass. The Outsunny states up to 12 inches, the Poulan Pro an intake of 10.5 inches, the Westinghouse and Snow Joe machines 10 inches, and the DEKOPRO 9 inches. Deeper snow than the intake height means clearing in layers. If you often get more than 8 inches at once, size up to a two stage machine.

Gas gives unlimited runtime for a fuel and maintenance cost, cordless gives silence and zero fuel for a limited runtime, and corded gives unlimited runtime tied to an outlet. The Poulan Pro is the gas pick, the Westinghouse WSnow18, Outsunny and Snow Joe are the cordless picks, and the Westinghouse WSnow18D and DEKOPRO are the corded picks. Pick the type that matches the length of your drive and your tolerance for upkeep.

The auger is the only part that touches the pavement. A rubber-tipped steel auger, like the one on the Westinghouse WSnow18, scrapes without gouging. A polyurethane auger, like the Outsunny's, is gentler still on decks and pavers. A plain steel auger, like the DEKOPRO's, needs more care. Check the auger type before buying for a deck, paver patio or gravel.

Cordless runtime is the number that decides whether a blower finishes your driveway. The Westinghouse WSnow18 states about 15 minutes for 7 inches of snow and a 1.8 hour charge, and the Outsunny charges in about 2 hours. Cold reduces battery output, so keep batteries indoors until use. For a long driveway, buy a second set of batteries.

Throw distance decides where the snow ends up and whether you need to clear it twice. The Westinghouse machines throw up to 25 feet, the Snow Joe 20 feet and the Outsunny 21.3 feet. The Poulan Pro adds a one hand 190 degree remote chute, and the Outsunny adds a 60 degree vertical pitch. Wind and wet snow shorten the real throw.

A machine that will not start on the morning you need it is no help. The Poulan Pro adds electric start and cold start technology down to -22 F, and the WSnow18D has a push button start that works in cold weather. The Westinghouse machines have dual LED lights, which help in the dark. Check the start system before the first storm of the season.

specDecoder.meaning: The width of the path cut in one pass and the maximum snow depth the intake can take. A single stage blower throws snow with the same auger that scrapes the surface.
specDecoder.watchFor: Depth is for fresh, light snow. Wet or packed snow needs shallower passes than the listing implies.

specDecoder.meaning: A rate figure showing how fast the machine moves snow under ideal conditions, such as the 650, 720 and 800 pounds per minute on the Westinghouse and DEKOPRO listings.
specDecoder.watchFor: Manufacturers measure under different conditions, so compare rates only within the same brand.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without carbon brushes that wear out. It runs cooler and uses battery charge more efficiently.
specDecoder.watchFor: Brushless does not mean unlimited runtime. Battery capacity still decides how long it runs.

specDecoder.meaning: A set of engine features, such as a choke and throttle curve, that help a gas engine fire in freezing weather. The Poulan Pro lists starting to -22 F.
specDecoder.watchFor: It does not replace fresh fuel. Old gasoline is the usual reason a snow blower will not start.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum distance the discharge travels in ideal conditions, listed as 20, 21.3 or 25 feet in this lineup.
specDecoder.watchFor: Wind, wet snow and slow auger speed shorten the real distance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clearing capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared clearing width, depth and published snow rates, from the 9 inch depth of the DEKOPRO to the 12 inch depth of the Outsunny and the rates of 650 to 800 pounds per minute. Figures are manufacturer stated and treated as best case.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared gas, battery and corded power. For batteries we looked at stated runtime and charge time, such as 15 minutes for 7 inches and 1.8 hours on the Westinghouse WSnow18. We considered cold weather performance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Surface protection
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared auger materials: rubber-tipped steel on the Westinghouse and Poulan Pro, polyurethane on the Outsunny and plain steel on the DEKOPRO. Surface protection matters on decks, pavers and gravel.

howWeEvaluated.title: Starting and controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared electric start, push button starts, dual action safety switches and chute controls, including the 190 degree remote chute on the Poulan Pro and the vertical pitch on the Outsunny. Lights were considered for dark mornings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated warranty terms: two years on the Poulan Pro and Westinghouse, with lifetime technical support on the Westinghouse. Machines without stated warranty terms in the data we have were ranked lower for support confidence.

howToChoose.intro: The basic tradeoff in single stage blowers.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: A gas engine runs as long as there is fuel, starts in deep cold with the right technology and handles heavier snow. It needs fuel, stabilizer and seasonal maintenance. The Poulan Pro 18 Inch Gas Snow Blower is the gas pick.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: Cordless and corded machines are quiet, emission free and need no engine maintenance. Cordless runtime and cord reach are the limits. The Westinghouse WSnow18, Outsunny, Snow Joe, Westinghouse WSnow18D and DEKOPRO are the electric picks.

howToChoose.note: Pick gas if your driveway is long or the snow is heavy. Pick electric for short drives, quiet and low upkeep.

howToChoose.subheading: For Paved Driveways and Decks Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A rubber-tipped or polyurethane auger that protects the surface, and an intake height that suits your usual snowfall. If you have gravel, check for an adjustable skid shoe, which keeps the auger off the stones. Avoid steel augers on decks.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Outsunny 40V 18 Inch Snow Blower, with its PU auger, is the gentlest on decks and pavers. The Westinghouse WSnow18 and the Poulan Pro use rubber-tipped or rubber augers that suit pavement.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your driveway is long, snow is heavy or you want a machine that starts in deep cold. The Poulan Pro 18 Inch Gas Snow Blower is the pick, and the Westinghouse WSnow18 is the best cordless upgrade.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your clearing area is small and near an outlet. The DEKOPRO or the Westinghouse WSnow18D corded machines cost less and need no fuel or batteries.

howToChoose.note: If your driveway is long or steep, or snow regularly exceeds a foot, a two stage machine is the right tool.

maintenance.task: Check fuel and oil before the first storm
maintenance.why: Old gasoline is the usual reason a snow blower will not start. Drain stale fuel and refill with fresh, stabilized fuel and check the oil level.
Lithium ion batteries lose output in deep cold. Keep them in a dry place at room temperature and charge before the forecast.
A worn rubber paddle or scraper bar stops clearing to the pavement. Replace worn parts before the season.
A nicked cord is a shock risk. Use a GFCI protected outlet and an outdoor rated extension cord.
Packed snow and salt cause rust and freeze the chute. Clear the chute with a stick, not your hand, and let the machine dry.

faq.q: Is an 18 inch snow blower enough for my driveway?
faq.a: An 18 inch machine suits small to medium driveways, sidewalks and decks with light to moderate snow, and is easy to handle. It takes more passes than a wider machine. For a long driveway or snow over about 10 inches, consider a wider or two stage model.

faq.q: How much should I budget for a snow blower?
faq.a: Corded machines cost the least, cordless kits cost more and the gas machine sits at the upper end here. Cordless kits may need a second set of batteries and gas needs fuel and maintenance. Compare the total cost of ownership, not only the price.

faq.q: How long do cordless snow blower batteries last?
faq.a: Runtime per charge is short, about 15 minutes for 7 inches of snow on the Westinghouse WSnow18. Battery life across seasons depends on storage and use. Keep batteries indoors and charge them before a storm.

faq.q: Can a single stage blower handle wet snow?
faq.a: It can, but wet snow is heavier, throws shorter and needs shallower passes. Rate and depth claims describe light snow. For frequent wet snow, a gas machine or a two stage model is better.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a snow blower?
faq.a: Never put your hand in the chute, and use a stick to clear a clog after the machine is stopped and the power is disconnected or the key removed. Wear eye and hearing protection. Use a GFCI outlet with corded machines.

faq.q: Will a snow blower damage gravel or decks?
faq.a: A single stage blower's auger contacts the surface and can throw stones from gravel. Use a machine with a rubber-tipped or PU auger on pavement and decks, and raise the skid shoe on gravel.
